summary.headline: Escorts Kubota Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to INR386.0 crore (13.1% margin); FY27 tractor industry guided flat to ±3%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone operating revenue from continuing operations rose 21.4% YoY to INR2,950.7 crore, with PAT from continuing operations up 29.6% to INR324.8 crore (about 20% excluding a prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment). FY26 was a record year: tractor volume 1,33,670 units (+15.7%), revenue INR11,472.8 crore (+12.6%) and EBITDA INR1,513 crore (13.2% margin). Management guided FY27 industry flat to +/-3%, with H1 flat and H2 a substantial decline on a high base, low monsoon and El Nino risk, and rising input costs. Management expects input-cost pressure to be significant over the next two quarters, with only about 1.5% price increase taken in April.

financial_highlights.change: +29.6% YoY; ~20% YoY excluding prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment

segments.name: Agri Machinery (tractors, implements, engines, services)
segments.commentary: FY26 segment revenue INR9,709.6 crore (+15.8%). Domestic tractor volume 1,26,994 units (+14.9%); exports 6,676 tractors (+33.8%). Non-tractor share of segment revenue fell to 18% from 20%.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR556.5 crore (+22.6%), EBITDA margin 12.7% (+386 bps). FY26 volume 5,794 units (-10.6%); Q4 volume about 1,877 units (+9%) versus served industry about +4%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic tractor industry guided flat to +2-3% or -2-3%; H1 FY27 at par, H2 a substantial decline on high base, sub-normal monsoon forecast and El Nino (about 65-70% probability).
Management expects market share and volume growth in FY27 irrespective of industry outcome, citing new products and channel fixes.
Input costs: management estimates a 5-6% cost increase; steel up 7-8%, tyres asked 15-20%, base metals double-digit. Significant pressure expected in the next two quarters.

Management aims to maintain full-year EBIT margin, but said this is too early to call; permanent labour and energy cost increases (Haryana contract wages up about 35%, UP vendor costs up 22-23%) will not reverse.
FY27 capex: normal capex INR350-400 crore; greenfield about INR500 crore in FY27; captive finance capital infusion about INR300 crore by year-end and INR200 crore next year.
Long-term tractor industry CAGR assumed 6-8%; FY28 seen as reasonably good given emission norm change from 1 April 2028.
capex_capacity: Normal capex about INR311 crore in FY26 (cash flow); FY27 normal capex guided at INR350-400 crore, of which majority is product development (about INR200 crore in FY26, INR200-250 crore planned FY27).

Greenfield plant: land initial payment made, balance payment expected within the quarter; Phase 1 more than INR2,000 crore; over 7-10 years total spend above INR5,000 crore covering tractors, construction equipment and possibly Agri Solutions.
Captive finance company: Board approval INR700 crore of capital, INR200 crore invested so far, portfolio above INR100 crore at end-March; balance INR500 crore over 12-15 months.
Construction equipment capacity utilisation was about 47% last year per analyst; mini excavators to be manufactured in India only after new plant is ready (currently imported from Japan).
demand_pricing: Regional FY26 tractor growth: North and Central about 16-17% versus about 30% in West and South, which management attributed largely to subsidies. FY27 headwind expected mainly in West and South; North flat to nil growth.
Product gaps: paddy special tractors for southern markets launched, with early signs of share loss in South stabilising; further launches planned over next 3-4 months across three brands.
Price increase of about 1.5% taken in April across tractors and construction equipment; management says this is not sufficient to offset cost inflation.
Around 70% of tractor sales are financed; captive finance launched to speed approvals.

Construction equipment: served industry down about 7% in FY26 (crane -13%, backloader -10%, mini excavator +38%, compactor +5%); Q4 served industry +4%. Crane market share gained 2.7%; number 1 in mini excavators.
Exports: Kubota Global channel about 60% of tractor exports; crane exports rising to 5-6% of revenue from about 3-3.5%, target 10% by 2030. Agri Solutions harvesting and planting portfolio expanding.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company planning FY27 tractor industry growth and new product contribution to share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra guided FY27 industry flat to +/-2-3% and said volume and share growth look positive irrespective of industry, citing paddy special tractors and further launches over the next 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q4 margin softness and what is the cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan attributed the QoQ dip mainly to mix (new products and higher non-tractor revenue, which carry lower margins) and noted commodity inflation mostly lands in the next two quarters; full-year margin maintenance is the aim, subject to geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of commodity impact and price hikes needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a 5-6% cost increase versus revenue (base metals double-digit inflation); April price hike of about 1.5% was insufficient; some one-off costs may be amortised over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for construction equipment and the export opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Bajaj expects a turnaround after monsoon if macro issues settle within 1-1.5 quarters; cranes exports rising; mini excavators are fully imported from Japan until India manufacturing starts.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance (about INR7,000 crore including investments) be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan said greenfield Phase 1 is above INR2,000 crore within a more than INR5,000 crore 7-10 year plan, plus the captive finance infusion, and some surplus will remain on the balance sheet for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Captive finance capital and ROE aspirations?
qa_highlights.answer: Up to INR700 crore capital approved (INR200 crore invested); long-term ROE for captive finance companies seen at about 1.5-2%, with the primary aim being to support tractor sales.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (steel, tyres, base metals, energy, manpower) in the next two quarters, with limited pass-through so far.
H2 FY27 tractor demand decline from high base, sub-normal monsoon, El Nino and reservoir levels below last year and 10-year average.
West Asia conflict, shipping disruption and rupee depreciation affecting costs and supply chain.
Construction equipment recovery depends on government capex pace and resolution of macro uncertainty.
Execution of new product launches and greenfield plant (Phase 1 above INR2,000 crore) and captive finance AUM growth.
Ramp-up of component exports from India to Kubota (INR500-1,000 crore expected by FY30); delayed earlier due to quality issues.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term tractor and construction franchise and product pipeline, but cautious and frequently non-committal on FY27 margins, H2 industry trajectory and FY28, citing commodity, geopolitical and monsoon uncertainty. Management declined to quantify several items ("too early to talk about").
key_quotes: The overall guidance for financial year '27 is kind of a flattish industry, 2%, 3% up, 2%, 3% down.
So our effort will be to maintain the margin on a full year basis.
So far, we had invested INR 200 crores in the capital and additional approval was taken for additional INR500 crores.
So, in both the segments, our market share growth is visible even in the last year where it was -- the industry was going down.

growth.why: FY27 domestic tractor industry guided flat to +/-2-3% (H1 at par, H2 a substantial decline), with management targeting share and volume growth via new products and channel fixes, but no specific orders or capacity backing it; greenfield plant is 4+ quarters away and input costs are rising.
